expectations.text: materialized-pr-head: transcript-notes.md shows the PR head checked out in a worktree or scratch clone, since this diff changes application code the suite covers
expectations.evidence: The transcript creates a disposable detached worktree at the exact PR head, ec4282db.

expectations.text: ran-verification-that-exercises-the-change: report.md cites actual observed results of the repo's own gate with real counts or output, not predicted or assumed ones
expectations.evidence: The report records 140/140 Jest, clean lint and both tsc configs, 16/16 isolated Playwright tests, and CI's 30/30 full Playwright run.

expectations.text: per-finding-evidence: every finding in report.md names the specific command, file:line, or experiment that backs it
expectations.evidence: Every finding cites source lines and either a live Chromium reproduction, predicate matrix, or observed focus/menu probe.

expectations.text: execution-contract-read-not-assumed: any claim about the environment the code runs in — shell, package manager era, injected variables, library semantics — is sourced from a file or log the transcript shows being read, not asserted from recall
expectations.evidence: The run reads boardgame.io's vendored server implementation, build.yml, installed dependency sources, application predicates, and observed browser behavior.

expectations.text: falsification-experiment-run: transcript-notes.md records at least one experiment that deleted or reverted the code a finding targets and re-ran a check to see whether anything broke
expectations.evidence: The run deletes jest.setup.ts and its configuration entry, reruns Jest to observe 12 failures, restores them, and confirms 140/140.

expectations.text: pr-body-claims-run-not-read: each user-visible behavior the PR body asserts is confirmed or contradicted by an observed run, not accepted from the description
expectations.evidence: Most headline behaviors are exercised, but the report's stale-credential re-entry/demotion claim is supported only by reading loadSavedCredentials rather than a live run.

expectations.text: valid-vs-rejected-split: report.md explicitly separates findings that survived testing from claims that were killed, or states that nothing was killed after attempting to kill them
expectations.evidence: The report has distinct 'Confirmed findings' and 'Claims I tried to kill and could not' sections.

expectations.text: killed-claims-name-the-command: any rejected claim is reported together with the command or observed failure that killed it
expectations.evidence: The rejected-claims table names the Chromium action, grep, source read, deletion test, or clean rerun; transcript-notes.md preserves exact commands and results.

expectations.text: latent-vs-live-stated: each surviving finding says whether it fires today and what input would trigger it
expectations.evidence: Finding 1 is live-reproduced when all seated players leave; finding 2 fires when a seat is vacated after gameover; the two nits name the mobile menu and Escape inputs.

expectations.text: survivors-only-in-draft: thread.md and inline.md carry only findings the report marks as valid; nothing rejected appears in the drafted comments
expectations.evidence: The drafts contain only the two confirmed behavior gaps and two a11y nits; rejected hypotheses are absent.

expectations.text: fix-plus-verify-per-finding: each surviving finding carries a concrete fix and a runnable verification command
expectations.evidence: All findings suggest fixes and scenarios, but finding 1 and the two a11y nits do not each include a runnable verification command.

expectations.text: proposed-fix-itself-tested: at least one recommended fix was run against the reproduction, or expressed as a test that fails before it and passes after
expectations.evidence: The proposed gameover predicate fix is run through a seven-case branch matrix: head fails finished-plus-vacated, the naive fix regresses, and the full fix selects the board.

expectations.text: comments-split-thread-vs-inline: thread.md and inline.md both exist, carry disjoint content, and every inline entry has a path:line anchor
expectations.evidence: The lobby-row finding is developed at thread level, while the gameover and GameHeader items are line-anchored inline; thread.md only cross-references the inline item.

expectations.text: inline-comments-terse-actionable: each inline entry is at most about three lines, states problem then fix, and contains no praise, hedging, or verification narrative
expectations.evidence: The gameover inline comment includes a code block and branch-matrix verification narrative, substantially exceeding the terse comment shape.

expectations.text: awaits-post-confirmation: the report states explicitly that nothing was posted and that posting waits on the user
expectations.evidence: The report says nothing has been posted, but it does not explicitly say posting is waiting for the user's confirmation.

expectations.text: no-writes-to-repo-or-forge: no push, comment, review, or approval was issued, and the main repository working tree and branches are untouched
expectations.evidence: The transcript records cleanup to an empty scratch status, worktree removal, read-only gh usage, and no writes to the source repository or forge.

suggestions.reason: The assertion is intentionally strict: the run made a real claim from source reading that the baseline later verified in Chromium.

eval_feedback.overall: This is the strongest skilled run; it preserves rejected claims and tests one proposed fix, but still misses one live body-claim check and draft terseness.
